findings.body:
`_read_github_event_repo_visibility()` only reads `repository.visibility`. When that field is missing (older webhook payloads / some GHES versions still ship `private: true|false` without `visibility`), this returns `unknown`.

The permission override and private fail-open both require `_is_private_or_internal_visibility()`, so a real private org admin under-reported as `CONTRIBUTOR` is denied instead of allowed — the exact false-skip this PR aims to fix. Fall back to the boolean `private` field when `visibility` is absent.

`main()` calls `gh_get_collaborator_permission` whenever the webhook association is not in the allow-list, with **no visibility check**. On public repos the enhanced resolver correctly ignores write-tier permission, so the REST result is discarded — but every denied external PR still pays a GitHub API round-trip.

That contradicts the shipped docs/CHANGELOG claim that the lookup is private/internal-only, and weakens the “cheapest-first / zero cost on deny” abuse-prevention story on public repos (the gate’s primary threat model). Gate the lookup with `_is_private_or_internal_visibility(repo_visibility)` and leave `permission_lookup_failed=False` on public/unknown so association-only deny stays free.

This example still says empty `author-association` is “only sensible for private repos” and that the author gate is a pure payload read with no API call. Both statements are stale after Option B: private/internal should keep the default allow-list (permission fallback), and a mismatch may perform one collaborator-permission lookup.

AGENTS.md Rule #7 requires examples to stay aligned with runtime behaviour; leaving the old private-repo recommendation will push consumers back toward `author-association: ''` — the workaround this PR removes.

This callout still says a non-whitelisted author is skipped with “zero API cost”. After this change that is only true for public/association-only denies; private/internal mismatches may call the collaborator-permission API. Worth a one-line update so it matches `docs/SECURITY.md`.

summary:
Solid fix for a real private-org false-skip, with the right public-vs-private split in the pure resolver and good unit coverage of the decision matrix. A few wiring/docs gaps still undercut the intended contract.

### What works
- `resolve_author_association_gate_enhanced` correctly keeps public repos association-only, allows `admin`/`maintain`/`write` only on private/internal, and fail-opens vs fail-closes by visibility as documented.
- Username is `urllib.parse.quote`d; 404 → `none` (not lookup failure); broad `except` is annotated with the approved BLE001 pattern.
- Docs surface is mostly in sync: `action.yml`, README, SECURITY, CHANGELOG, setup skill + reference.
- New `AuthorAssociationGatePermissionTests` cover the important branches (including public write not widening a strict gate).

### Gaps worth fixing before merge
1. **`repository.visibility` only** — if the webhook omits `visibility` (but still has `private: true`), the gate treats the repo as `unknown` and never applies the private override/fail-open. Prefer falling back to the boolean `private` field.
2. **Lookup not visibility-gated in `main()`** — every association miss currently hits the collaborators/permission API, including public external PRs where the result is ignored. That burns the “cheapest-first / zero cost on deny” property the gate is sold on; gate the call to private/internal only.
3. **`examples/open-source-safe.yml` still teaches the old private-repo empty-gate workaround** and “no API call” wording — contradicts the new SECURITY guidance and AGENTS.md Rule #7.
4. **`docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md`** still says “zero API cost” for author-gate skips (info).

No critical security/contract breaks found (no new non-stdlib imports, no input renames, path/env allowlist untouched). Self-review dogfood is still unchecked in the PR body — worth running once the wiring fixes land.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
